newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco's Chuquicamata normal after heavy rains.
newsitem.headline: Codelco's Chuquicamata normal after heavy rains.

text.p: Codelco's Chuquicamata mine in Northern Chile was working normally again on Saturday after rains and wind paralysed production on Friday, officials for the state mining company said.
The mine may use September's two-day national holidays to make up for lost output, they added.
A freak rainstorm on Friday shut the mine intermittently for a total of nearly eight hours Friday and knocked out electricity for a few hours, officials said.
Work did not fully resume until about 11 p.m. (0300 GMT Saturday), they said.
"We lost a complete shift. We're planning to make up for it during the Independence Day holidays" on September 18 and 19, said one official.
"The rain and the wind made all the operations very difficult ... finally it was decided to stop work," he added. "We're back up to 100 percent now as of the first Saturday shift."
Work at Codelco's nearby Radomiro Tomic copper prospect, now under construction and due for completion in early 1998, was also paralysed by the weather, local radio reports said.
